html:
The birdman cult was the religion of Rapa Nui after the age of the moai. Each spring, men raced down the cliffs of the Orongo crater, swam to the islet of Motu Nui and waited for the first sooty tern egg of the season.

The chief whose man brought back the egg became tangata manu, the birdman, for a year, with special rights and honour. The god Makemake was its centre, and the rocks at Orongo are covered with carvings of birdmen.

The rite ended in the 1860s, after the slave raids and the arrival of Catholic missionaries. The rongorongo tablets may come from the same period.
